question: In round 5, when you first ran the PT_PROF cost-share sweep with the scratch profiling build in _prof/, it printed no timings. What was wrong?
answer:
The sweep printed nothing because the profiling build never rendered a frame: its Metal source failed to compile at startup, and my sweep command hid the reason by sending stderr to /dev/null.

What was wrong concretely: my PT_PROF patch for bit 2 ("skip the mesh closest-hit walk") read `params.pad` inside `pt_intersect_scene` in _prof/shaders/pt_trace.metal, but that function has no local `params` — it reaches the per-frame parameters through `scene.params`. So the runtime MSL compile failed with `program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'`, the host printed `metal init error: shader compile failed: ...` to stderr and exited before tracing. Because the shaders are compiled by newLibraryWithSource at startup, the clang++ build itself succeeded (the _prof binary existed, 102,104 bytes), and with `2>/dev/null | tail -1` each loop iteration just echoed `PT_PROF=<n>` followed by an empty captured line, with exit code 0 — so the failure looked like missing timings rather than a crash.

How I know: the first sweep [#52] shows six empty `PT_PROF=` lines; running one invocation directly with stderr shown [#54] printed the `use of undeclared identifier 'params'` compile error plus `metal init error: shader compile failed`; changing that line to `scene.params->pad` [#55] fixed it with no rebuild (shaders compile at runtime), and the same sweep then produced the cost shares [#58]: full 45.612/45.352ms, no-shadow 44.252/44.051, no-NEE 43.348/43.171, glass-always-reflect 35.965/35.764, no-mesh 4.939/4.773, no-mesh+no-shadow 0.623/0.458 — the measurement that showed the BVH closest-hit walk is ~89% of the frame. Two lessons I have kept since: a kernel error is invisible to the build command, so never discard stderr when a run prints nothing, and always confirm the binary actually emits a benchmark line before trusting a comparison (the same class of bug later made a silent A/B base look like a win).

question: In round 5, when you first ran the PT_PROF cost-share sweep with the scratch profiling build in _prof/, it printed no timings. What was wrong?
answer:

What was wrong: my PT_PROF patch for bit 2 ("skip mesh closest-hit") was written into pt_intersect_scene in _prof/shaders/pt_trace.metal as `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && ...)`, but that function has no local `params` — it reaches the parameters through the scene struct. The general lesson I recorded: since shaders compile at runtime, a shader bug looks like an empty result unless stderr is kept; always verify a reference binary actually prints a benchmark line before trusting an A/B or sweep.

question: In round 5, when you first ran the PT_PROF cost-share sweep with the scratch profiling build in _prof/, it printed no timings. What was wrong?
answer:
The sweep printed nothing because the profiling build's Metal source did not compile, and my loop threw the error message away.

What was wrong: the PT_PROF guard I had just added to _prof/shaders/pt_trace.metal was written as `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && pt_intersect_mesh(...))` inside pt_intersect_scene, but that function has no local named `params` — it reaches the parameters through `scene.params`. So the kernel source had an undeclared identifier.

Why that produced silence instead of a build failure: this project has no offline `metal` compiler, so the host compiles the shaders at startup with newLibraryWithSource. The clang++ build of the C++/Obj-C++ side succeeded (it never sees the .metal text), and each binary then bailed during init with `metal init error: shader compile failed: program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'`. That text goes to stderr, and my sweep command sent stderr to /dev/null and kept only `tail -1` of stdout, so all six PT_PROF lines came out blank (#52). I only saw the real cause when I re-ran a single invocation with stderr visible (#54).

Fix and confirmation: changed the guard to `scene.params->pad` (#55-#56). No rebuild was needed because the shaders are compiled at runtime, and the same sweep then produced the cost shares I recorded — full 45.35ms gpu_ms_best, no-shadow 44.05, no-NEE 43.17, no-mesh 4.77, i.e. the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame (#58).

The general lesson I logged: a silent benchmark line means the base binary probably failed to initialize — always check that the reference binary prints a benchmark line, and never discard stderr when a run comes back empty. (Evidence: messages #51, #52, #53, #54, #55, #58.)

After fixing the layout (headers in <dir>/include, shaders in <dir>/shaders next to the binary) the same PT_PROF build did print the cost shares I later used (full 45.35ms; no-shadow 44.05; no-NEE 43.17; no-mesh 4.77, i.e. the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame). The general lesson I now apply to every scratch/A/B build: check that the base binary prints a benchmark line before trusting any measurement from it.
